text: The business has a written plan for the next 12 months that sets sales and profit targets.
anchor0: No plan exists; direction is only in the owner's head
anchor1: Owner can describe goals verbally but nothing is written
anchor2: Written plan lists activities but has no numbers for sales or profit
anchor3: Written plan states sales and profit targets in cedis
anchor4: Written plan with targets, updated within the last 12 months with changes recorded
evidenceRequirement: Ask to see the current plan and check it has numeric targets and a date of last update.
evidenceExamples: Business plan or annual plan document | Notebook page with dated sales and profit targets

text: Staff who run sales, production or service can state the current target for their own area.
anchor0: No targets exist for any area of the business
anchor1: Owner has targets in mind but staff do not know them
anchor2: Some staff can state a target when asked
anchor3: All staff in charge of an area can state their target
anchor4: All can state their target and the latest result against it
evidenceRequirement: Ask two or three staff or helpers, separately, what their target is and how they are doing against it.
evidenceExamples: Shop attendant states daily sales target | Production lead states weekly output target and last week's result

text: Before any large spend on equipment, stock or expansion, the owner writes down the cost, the expected extra income and the payback time.
anchor0: Large purchases are made on impulse with no calculation
anchor1: Owner thinks about the benefit but writes nothing down
anchor2: Cost is written but expected return is not
anchor3: Cost, expected extra income and payback time are written for the last large spend
anchor4: Written for every large spend in 12 months and actual results later compared
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the calculation behind the last large purchase or expansion and check it was done before the spend.
evidenceExamples: Page showing machine cost, extra sales expected and months to recover cost | Quotation with owner's handwritten payback calculation

text: The business has customers who come back to buy again, and the records can show this.
anchor0: No repeat buyers, or no sales record that could show any
anchor1: Owner says some customers return but cannot name any
anchor2: Owner can name three to five repeat customers
anchor3: Records show more than five customers who bought in at least two of the last six months
anchor4: Repeat customers account for over half of sales and repeat orders grew over the last 12 months
evidenceRequirement: Check sales records for the same customers buying in different months and ask two customers by phone.
evidenceExamples: Customer ledger showing repeat orders | Mobile money history with repeat payers | Call to two named customers

text: In the last 12 months the business changed a product, service or delivery method because customers told it what they wanted.
anchor0: Never asks customers and has changed nothing
anchor1: Hears complaints but changes nothing
anchor2: Asked customers once and noted views without acting
anchor3: Made one change after customer feedback and can say what it was
anchor4: Made several changes from feedback and checked sales or satisfaction afterwards
evidenceRequirement: Ask for a specific change, its date and the feedback behind it, and check with a customer if possible.
evidenceExamples: New pack size after buyers asked for smaller units | Opening hours changed after customer survey notes

text: The business can say clearly why customers choose it over a competitor, and customers give the same reason when asked.
anchor0: Cannot say why customers choose it
anchor1: Gives only a general reason such as good quality or low price
anchor2: Gives one specific reason but customers have not confirmed it
anchor3: Gives a specific reason and two of three customers called give the same one
anchor4: Specific reason confirmed by customers and used in the business's selling or marketing
evidenceRequirement: Ask the owner for the reason, then ask three customers why they buy from the business.
evidenceExamples: Customers say the business delivers same day | Banner or social media post stating the main reason

text: A written plan says how and where new customers will be found this year.
anchor0: No plan to find new customers
anchor1: Owner has ideas but nothing is written
anchor2: Written list of ideas with no person or dates
anchor3: Written plan with actions, a responsible person and dates
anchor4: Written plan, actions carried out and the number of new customers recorded
evidenceRequirement: Ask to see the plan and the count of new customers won against it.
evidenceExamples: Marketing plan with named actions | Notebook list of target buyers with visit dates

text: The business keeps a list of customer names and phone numbers and uses it to reach customers directly.
anchor0: No customer list exists
anchor1: Numbers are only on the owner's phone and are not used
anchor2: A list exists but is used rarely
anchor3: List is kept up to date and used at least monthly, for example a WhatsApp broadcast list
anchor4: List includes purchase history and is used for targeted offers with results noted
evidenceRequirement: Ask to see the list and a recent message or call log showing how it was used.
evidenceExamples: WhatsApp Business broadcast list | Customer contact notebook | Spreadsheet of customers and last purchase

text: Share of sales in the last 12 months that came from the single largest customer.
anchor0: Above 60 percent, or the share is not known
anchor1: 41 to 60 percent
anchor2: 31 to 40 percent
anchor3: 16 to 30 percent
anchor4: 15 percent or less
evidenceRequirement: Calculate the largest customer's share from the sales ledger, invoices or payment history.
evidenceExamples: Sales ledger totals by customer | Invoice register for the last 12 months

text: The business knows which way of reaching customers (referral, shop location, WhatsApp, social media, radio, agents) brings the most new customers.
anchor0: No deliberate marketing and no idea how customers arrive
anchor1: Does some marketing but has no idea which part works
anchor2: Owner estimates the best channel from memory
anchor3: Asks new customers how they heard and has counts for the last three months
anchor4: Counts new customers by channel monthly and has moved effort or money to the best channel
evidenceRequirement: Ask for counts of new customers by source and an example of a decision based on them.
evidenceExamples: Tally of 'how did you hear about us' answers | Social media page insights with enquiry counts

text: The price of each main product or service is set from its cost plus a target margin.
anchor0: Prices are guessed or copied without any cost calculation
anchor1: Prices follow competitors only; cost is not worked out
anchor2: Cost is roughly worked out for the main items only
anchor3: Prices come from a written cost plus margin for all main items
anchor4: As before, and the sheet is dated and updated at least twice a year or when input costs change
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the costing sheet behind two main prices and check the date.
evidenceExamples: Costing sheet with ingredients, labour, transport and margin | Spreadsheet with cost and selling price per item

text: How often does the owner check competitors' prices and offers?
anchor0: Never checks competitors
anchor1: Rarely, only when customers complain about price
anchor2: Sometimes, about once a year, from memory
anchor3: Often, at least every six months, with notes
anchor4: Always, every quarter, in a written comparison used when setting prices
evidenceRequirement: Ask when the last check was done and for any notes or comparison.
evidenceExamples: Notebook of competitor prices with dates | Photos of competitor price lists

text: Discounts and price reductions are given under a rule, not case by case on request.
anchor0: Discounts are given freely with no limit
anchor1: Owner decides case by case and nothing is recorded
anchor2: An informal limit exists that only the owner knows
anchor3: A written rule exists and sales staff know it
anchor4: Written rule applied, discounts recorded and their total cost reviewed monthly
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the discount rule and a record of discounts given last month.
evidenceExamples: Written discount policy | Sales book with a discount column

text: Orders are delivered on the agreed day and to the agreed specification.
anchor0: Orders are often late or wrong and no record is kept
anchor1: More than one in five orders is late or wrong, according to customers
anchor2: Orders are sometimes late or wrong and this is not tracked
anchor3: Orders are rarely late or wrong and late orders are noted
anchor4: On-time and correct rate is tracked monthly and is above 90 percent
evidenceRequirement: Ask two buyers about reliability and check any delivery or order log.
evidenceExamples: Buyer confirms deliveries arrive on time | Delivery book with dates promised and dates delivered

text: Products or work are checked against a stated standard before they reach the customer.
anchor0: No checks are done
anchor1: Checks happen only when the owner is present
anchor2: Checks are usually done but nothing is written
anchor3: A written checklist exists and is used for most sales or jobs
anchor4: Checklist is used for every batch or job, failures are recorded and causes fixed
evidenceRequirement: Observe a check being done and look at the checklist and failure records.
evidenceExamples: Quality checklist at the packing table | Inspection sheet signed before dispatch

text: Customer complaints, returns and refunds are written down and followed up.
anchor0: Complaints are ignored or not handled
anchor1: Complaints are handled informally and forgotten
anchor2: The owner remembers complaints but nothing is written
anchor3: A written log exists with the action taken
anchor4: Log records cause and action, complaints are closed within an agreed time and patterns reviewed
evidenceRequirement: Ask to see the complaints or returns log for the last three months.
evidenceExamples: Complaints notebook | WhatsApp complaint messages with replies and outcome

text: The main products or services are made or delivered by following set steps, so different staff produce the same result.
anchor0: Every person does the work their own way and results differ widely
anchor1: Only the owner knows the right way
anchor2: Steps are shown to new staff by demonstration but not written
anchor3: Steps are written or illustrated for the main product or service
anchor4: Steps are written, staff are trained on them and they were updated in the last 12 months
evidenceRequirement: Watch two staff do the same task and compare with any written steps.
evidenceExamples: Recipe or production sheet on the wall | Step list for a standard repair or service

text: Stock, materials or supplies on hand are physically counted and compared with the stock records.
anchor0: Stock is never counted
anchor1: Counted once a year or only when a problem appears
anchor2: Counted every two to three months
anchor3: Counted every month and compared with records
anchor4: Counted every month, differences investigated and the cause recorded
evidenceRequirement: Observe or ask for the latest count sheet and the record it was compared with.
evidenceExamples: Stock count sheet signed by two people | Stock book with count date and variance column

text: Each key input or item for resale can be bought from at least two known suppliers.
anchor0: Depends on one supplier and knows no alternative
anchor1: One main supplier; alternatives have never been checked
anchor2: An alternative supplier is named but has not been used
anchor3: Two suppliers have been used in the last six months for each key input
anchor4: As before, and prices from suppliers are compared in writing at least twice a year
evidenceRequirement: Review purchase records for each key input and ask for alternative supplier contacts.
evidenceExamples: Purchase book showing two suppliers per item | Written supplier price comparison

text: Waste, spoilage, breakage or loss is measured as a share of what is bought or produced.
anchor0: Not measured and the owner cannot estimate it
anchor1: Estimated from memory only
anchor2: Recorded occasionally for the main item
anchor3: Recorded every month for the main items
anchor4: Recorded monthly with causes noted, and losses are falling or below a set target
evidenceRequirement: Ask for loss records and check how the percentage is worked out.
evidenceExamples: Spoilage book | Production sheet showing input quantity and good output

text: Each month the main cost lines (inputs, transport, power, rent, wages) are compared with the previous month and rises are explained.
anchor0: Costs are never compared
anchor1: Costs are looked at only when cash runs short
anchor2: Owner notices big changes informally
anchor3: Main cost lines are compared monthly and rises are queried
anchor4: Compared monthly against a budget or target and corrective action is recorded
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the last two months' cost comparison and the action taken on any rise.
evidenceExamples: Spreadsheet with monthly cost columns | Notebook comparing fuel and input costs

text: Equipment and vehicles are serviced on a planned schedule rather than only after they break down.
anchor0: Repairs only after breakdown
anchor1: Servicing happens when someone remembers
anchor2: Informal schedule for the main items
anchor3: Written schedule for main assets and mostly followed
anchor4: Schedule followed, service log kept and breakdown time recorded
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the service schedule and log and inspect one key machine or vehicle.
evidenceExamples: Vehicle service book | Machine maintenance card with dates

text: The business keeps a list of its equipment and other assets with purchase cost, date and condition.
anchor0: No list exists
anchor1: The owner lists assets only from memory
anchor2: A list of main items exists without values
anchor3: A list shows cost, purchase date, condition and location
anchor4: List is checked physically at least yearly and updated, with serial or chassis numbers
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the asset list and tick three items from the list at the premises.
evidenceExamples: Fixed asset register | Spreadsheet of machines with purchase receipts attached

text: Output or work completed per worker or per day is measured for the main product or service.
anchor0: Not measured
anchor1: Estimated from memory
anchor2: Counted occasionally
anchor3: Counted every week for the main product or service
anchor4: Counted routinely, compared with a target and acted on
evidenceRequirement: Ask for output counts for the last four weeks and any target.
evidenceExamples: Daily production tally sheet | Jobs completed per technician record

text: The main work process has no regular bottleneck that delays orders.
anchor0: Orders are delayed every day by the same problem
anchor1: Orders are delayed weekly and nothing is done
anchor2: The bottleneck is known but there is no plan to fix it
anchor3: The bottleneck is known and a fix is in progress
anchor4: The bottleneck is solved, or capacity is checked each quarter against orders
evidenceRequirement: Walk the process with the owner and ask what slows orders most and what has been done.
evidenceExamples: Single dryer or machine causing queues | Order backlog list with reasons for delay

text: All cash and mobile money received and paid out is written in a cash book or other record every week.
anchor0: No record of money in or out is kept
anchor1: Only some sales are noted and not regularly
anchor2: Receipts and payments are recorded but more than a month behind
anchor3: Cash and mobile money in and out are recorded at least weekly
anchor4: Recorded daily and checked weekly against cash on hand and the mobile money or bank balance
evidenceRequirement: Inspect the cash book or spreadsheet for the last eight weeks and check entry dates against statements.
evidenceExamples: Cash book with weekly totals | Spreadsheet matching mobile money statement entries

text: Business money is kept separate from the owner's household and personal money.
anchor0: Business and personal money are in the same pocket, wallet or account
anchor1: Sometimes separate, but the owner takes cash freely with no record
anchor2: Separate account or wallet exists but personal use still happens and is not recorded
anchor3: Separate money, and the owner's withdrawals are recorded as drawings or salary
anchor4: Separate accounts, a fixed monthly owner pay, and no unrecorded personal withdrawals in the last three months
evidenceRequirement: Review three months of bank and mobile money statements for personal spending and compare with drawings records.
evidenceExamples: Business account statement with only business payments | Drawings page in the cash book

text: Sales and purchases are recorded in a ledger or software with the date, amount and the customer or supplier.
anchor0: No ledger exists
anchor1: Receipts and invoices are kept loosely but not recorded
anchor2: Sales are recorded but purchases are not
anchor3: Both sales and purchases are recorded with dates, amounts and names
anchor4: As before, and monthly totals agree with bank and mobile money statements
evidenceRequirement: Sample ten entries and trace them to receipts, invoices or statements.
evidenceExamples: Sales and purchases day books | Accounting software export

text: Receipts, invoices and waybills are filed so that any transaction in the last 12 months can be traced.
anchor0: No supporting documents are kept
anchor1: Some are kept loose and unsorted
anchor2: Kept in a box or bag but not sorted by date
anchor3: Filed by month and can be found when asked
anchor4: Filed and cross-referenced to ledger entries; five random transactions are found within ten minutes
evidenceRequirement: Pick five ledger entries at random and ask for the supporting document for each.
evidenceExamples: Monthly folders of receipts | Scanned invoices stored by date in a cloud folder

text: Weeks of fixed costs (rent, wages, loan repayments, power, transport) that cash on hand and in accounts could pay today.
anchor0: Less than 1 week of fixed costs, or the balance is not known
anchor1: 1 week to under 2 weeks
anchor2: 2 weeks to under 4 weeks
anchor3: 4 weeks to under 8 weeks
anchor4: 8 weeks or more
evidenceRequirement: Add cash, bank and mobile money balances on the day and divide by weekly fixed costs from the records.
evidenceExamples: Bank and mobile money balances shown on the day | Monthly fixed cost list

text: A written cash forecast shows the money expected in and out over the coming weeks.
anchor0: No forecast of any kind
anchor1: Owner thinks about upcoming cash but writes nothing
anchor2: A list of big upcoming payments only
anchor3: A written four week forecast updated at least monthly
anchor4: A rolling 13 week forecast updated every two weeks and compared with actual results
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the current forecast and the last update date.
evidenceExamples: Four week cash plan in a notebook | Spreadsheet forecast with actual columns

text: Average number of days customers take to pay on credit sales.
anchor0: Not known, or more than 60 days
anchor1: 46 to 60 days
anchor2: 31 to 45 days
anchor3: 16 to 30 days
anchor4: 15 days or fewer
evidenceRequirement: Compute from the list of unpaid invoices and recent payment dates.
evidenceExamples: Debtors list with invoice and payment dates | Customer credit book

text: The gross margin (sales less direct cost) is known for each main product or service.
anchor0: Not known at all
anchor1: Owner guesses an overall margin
anchor2: Calculated once for the whole business in the last year
anchor3: Calculated for each main product or service in the last six months
anchor4: Calculated for each main item every month and used in decisions
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the margin calculation for the top three items and check it uses real costs.
evidenceExamples: Margin per product table | Monthly gross margin worksheet

text: The monthly sales needed to cover all costs (break-even) has been calculated.
anchor0: Never heard of break-even and not calculated
anchor1: Owner has a vague idea of what sales are needed
anchor2: Rough estimate not based on records
anchor3: Calculated from fixed and variable costs in the last 12 months
anchor4: Calculated and compared with actual sales every month
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the calculation and check the fixed and variable costs used.
evidenceExamples: Break-even worksheet | Notebook page listing fixed costs and margin

text: Net profit or loss after all costs, including the owner's own pay, has been worked out for the last 12 months.
anchor0: Never worked out
anchor1: Owner estimates profit by feel
anchor2: Estimated from bank or mobile money movement only
anchor3: Worked out from records but without the owner's pay
anchor4: Worked out from records after owner's pay and tax, and the figure agrees with the books
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the profit calculation and check it against the ledger totals.
evidenceExamples: Income statement for last year | Profit and loss worksheet

text: Financial statements (income statement and balance sheet) have been prepared for the last full year.
anchor0: No financial statements have ever been prepared
anchor1: Owner has written a rough summary only
anchor2: A one page profit summary exists without a balance sheet
anchor3: Full statements prepared for the last year by the owner or a bookkeeper
anchor4: Statements prepared for the last two years and reviewed or audited by an external accountant
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the statements and check they cover a full year and balance.
evidenceExamples: Annual accounts prepared by an accountant | Statements drawn from accounting software

text: Payments above a set limit need approval from someone other than the person asking for the money.
anchor0: Anyone can pay out money freely
anchor1: The owner approves in theory but not in practice
anchor2: The owner approves verbally with no record
anchor3: A written limit exists and a named person approves above it
anchor4: Written limit, approvals are recorded and the owner checks them monthly
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the limit and look at three recent large payments for approval evidence.
evidenceExamples: Payment voucher with two signatures | Approval message on WhatsApp saved with the receipt

text: Cash, bank and mobile money balances are reconciled to the business records at least monthly.
anchor0: Never reconciled
anchor1: Only when an error is suspected
anchor2: Done about once a quarter
anchor3: Done every month by the owner
anchor4: Done every month by someone who does not record the money, with differences explained in writing
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the last three reconciliations and compare with statements.
evidenceExamples: Bank reconciliation statement | Cash count sheet matched to cash book and MoMo balance

text: All loans and supplier credit are repaid on or before the due date.
anchor0: Currently in default or in arrears of more than 90 days
anchor1: Late payments in the last 12 months with penalties charged
anchor2: One or two late payments in the last 12 months, no penalties
anchor3: All repayments on time in the last 12 months, shown by statements
anchor4: All repayments on time for 24 months with written repayment schedules
evidenceRequirement: Review loan statements or lender letters and supplier statements for the last 12 months.
evidenceExamples: Bank or microfinance loan statement | Supplier statement of account | Credit bureau report

text: Monthly cash available before loan repayments compared with the monthly loan repayments (debt cover).
anchor0: Below 1.0 times, or not known
anchor1: 1.0 to under 1.2 times
anchor2: 1.2 to under 1.5 times
anchor3: 1.5 to under 2.0 times
anchor4: 2.0 times or more
evidenceRequirement: Divide average monthly cash surplus before debt payments by monthly repayments using records.
evidenceExamples: Cash book summary and loan schedule | Bank statements and repayment schedule
riskTag: Loan repayments not covered by cash

text: The business keeps an up to date list of everything it owes (loans, supplier balances, advances) with amounts and due dates.
anchor0: No list of debts exists
anchor1: The owner knows the debts from memory only
anchor2: A list of loans exists but not supplier balances
anchor3: All debts are listed with amounts and due dates and updated monthly
anchor4: List updated monthly and checked against lender and supplier statements
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the list and check three items against a statement.
evidenceExamples: Creditors list | Loan schedule and supplier balances sheet

text: Borrowed money is used for stock, equipment or other items that earn income, not for routine shortfalls or personal spending.
anchor0: Loans mostly pay for personal or routine bills
anchor1: Sometimes used for personal or routine bills
anchor2: Mixed use, not tracked
anchor3: Used mainly for income earning items, shown by receipts
anchor4: Each loan has a written purpose and expected return before it is taken, and use was verified
evidenceRequirement: Trace the last loan's use through receipts and records.
evidenceExamples: Receipts for equipment bought with a loan | Loan application stating purpose, matched to spending

text: The business and its owner have no unresolved loan default, court judgement or blacklisting with a lender or credit bureau.
anchor0: In default or blacklisted now
anchor1: Arrears or a dispute is currently being renegotiated
anchor2: A past default has been fully cleared and the owner can show proof
anchor3: No default is known but this has not been checked with a bureau
anchor4: No default, confirmed by a credit report obtained in the last 12 months
evidenceRequirement: Ask for a credit report and lender clearance letters for any past default.
evidenceExamples: Credit bureau report | Lender letter confirming a loan is fully repaid

text: The owner has obtained a copy of their own credit report from a licensed credit bureau and checked it for errors.
anchor0: Has never heard of credit bureaus
anchor1: Knows bureaus exist but has not asked for a report
anchor2: Requested a report but did not review it
anchor3: Obtained and reviewed a report in the last 24 months
anchor4: Obtained a report in the last 12 months and challenged any errors in writing
evidenceRequirement: Ask to see the report and any dispute letter to the bureau.
evidenceExamples: Credit report printout | Dispute letter and bureau reply

text: The business or owner saves regularly in a bank, susu or VSLA for planned business needs.
anchor0: No regular saving
anchor1: Saves only occasionally
anchor2: Saves regularly but the money is mixed with personal funds
anchor3: Regular business saving in a separate account or group for at least six months
anchor4: Saved for 12 months or more and used for planned purchases or to part fund a loan, with records
evidenceRequirement: Ask for savings statements or the susu or VSLA book showing contributions.
evidenceExamples: Savings account statement | VSLA passbook | Susu collector's contribution card

text: The business has prepared and submitted a complete loan, grant or investment application in the last three years.
anchor0: Has never applied
anchor1: Applied but the application was incomplete or missing documents
anchor2: Submitted one complete application and kept no feedback
anchor3: Submitted a complete application and kept the lender or funder feedback
anchor4: Submitted more than one, used the feedback to improve, and at least one succeeded
evidenceRequirement: Ask for copies of applications and decision or feedback letters.
evidenceExamples: Loan application file | Grant proposal with acknowledgement | Rejection letter with reasons

text: A written funding plan states how much money is needed, for what, from which source and by when.
anchor0: No funding plan
anchor1: An amount is in the owner's mind but not written
anchor2: Amount and purpose are written without a source
anchor3: Amount, purpose, source and timing are written and costed
anchor4: As before, with supplier quotations and projected repayment or returns
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the funding plan and supporting quotations.
evidenceExamples: One page funding request | Quotation for equipment with a funding table

text: The business can show financial projections for the next 12 to 36 months with the assumptions written down.
anchor0: No projections
anchor1: Only a growth target without figures
anchor2: Sales projection only, without costs
anchor3: A 12 month projection of sales, costs and profit with assumptions
anchor4: A three year projection, monthly in year one, with assumptions compared with actual results
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the projection and check that its assumptions are stated and plausible.
evidenceExamples: Spreadsheet projection with an assumptions sheet | Business plan financial section

text: Who owns the business, and in what shares, is written down and can be shown.
anchor0: Ownership is unclear or disputed
anchor1: Only a verbal understanding exists
anchor2: Owners are known informally but nothing is written
anchor3: Ownership is recorded in a signed document or registration record
anchor4: As before, and the ownership filed with the Registrar General is up to date
evidenceRequirement: Ask for registration papers, partnership deed or shareholder records and check names match.
evidenceExamples: Company regulations and shareholder register | Business name registration certificate | Partnership agreement

text: The owner can put together a funder information pack (records, statements and registration documents) within one working day.
anchor0: Cannot be assembled
anchor1: Could be assembled within a week with great effort
anchor2: Could be assembled within two to three days
anchor3: Could be assembled within one day but is not kept together
anchor4: A ready folder, on paper or digital, was updated within the last six months
evidenceRequirement: Ask the owner to produce the pack now and time it.
evidenceExamples: Digital folder with certificates, statements and ledger summary | Box file with up to date documents

text: The business can run for a week without the owner on site, with sales and daily decisions continuing.
anchor0: The business stops or fails when the owner is away
anchor1: Major activities stop and customers are turned away
anchor2: Routine work continues but every decision waits for the owner
anchor3: Routine work and daily decisions are handled by a named deputy for a week
anchor4: This has happened in the last 12 months with no loss, and a written handover was used
evidenceRequirement: Ask staff and the deputy what happens when the owner travels or is ill and when it last occurred.
evidenceExamples: Deputy describes decisions taken during owner's absence | Handover note from the owner's last trip

text: A deputy or successor for the owner's role has been named in writing.
anchor0: No one has been considered
anchor1: The owner intends to name someone but has not
anchor2: Someone is named verbally and known to staff or family
anchor3: A successor or deputy is named in a signed or dated document
anchor4: Named in writing, briefed on key accounts and contacts, and has already acted in the role
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the document and interview the named person.
evidenceExamples: Letter naming a deputy | Board or family meeting minutes naming a successor

text: How often does the owner set aside time to work on the business (planning, review, improving), not only in it?
anchor0: Never; all time goes on daily tasks
anchor1: Rarely, only in a crisis
anchor2: Sometimes, about once a month
anchor3: Often, a weekly slot in the diary
anchor4: Always, a weekly slot with decisions or actions recorded
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the diary or notes showing the planning time and what was decided.
evidenceExamples: Weekly planning notes | Diary entry blocking Friday review time

text: In the last 12 months the owner changed a business practice after training, coaching or advice.
anchor0: No training or advice received and none sought
anchor1: Attended training but changed nothing
anchor2: Attended and tried one idea once
anchor3: Changed one practice and still uses it
anchor4: Changed several practices and measured the result
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the practice changed, the date, and evidence it is still used.
evidenceExamples: New cash book started after a bookkeeping workshop | Pricing sheet introduced after coaching visit

text: Every person's role and who they report to is written down.
anchor0: No roles are defined
anchor1: Roles are only understood verbally
anchor2: Written for some roles
anchor3: Written for all roles and known to staff
anchor4: Written, signed by staff and reviewed within the last 12 months
evidenceRequirement: Ask for role descriptions or an organisation chart and check staff know theirs.
evidenceExamples: Job descriptions | Simple organisation chart on the wall
applies: Has two or more people working in the business

text: People working in the business (staff, apprentices, helpers) are trained for their jobs when they join and when their tasks change.
anchor0: No training is given
anchor1: People learn by watching and there is no plan
anchor2: A basic induction is given to some people
anchor3: Induction for all new people and training when tasks change, recorded
anchor4: Annual training plan with a budget, and results checked against performance
evidenceRequirement: Ask for induction or training records and ask two people what training they received.
evidenceExamples: Training attendance list | Induction checklist signed by the new worker

text: People who perform well are recognised or rewarded in a clear and fair way.
anchor0: Same pay and no recognition whatever the performance
anchor1: Rewards go to favourites
anchor2: Occasional bonuses decided by the owner
anchor3: Criteria for rewards are known to staff and applied
anchor4: Written reward scheme with criteria, applied and reviewed each year
evidenceRequirement: Ask two staff how rewards are decided and ask for the criteria and recent examples.
evidenceExamples: Written bonus rules | Staff describe how the best seller was rewarded

text: The business knows how many people left in the last 12 months and why.
anchor0: No idea how many have left
anchor1: The owner recalls some leavers
anchor2: Count is known but not the reasons
anchor3: Count and reasons are recorded
anchor4: Recorded, and action was taken on a repeated reason
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the leaver list and reasons, and the action taken on any pattern.
evidenceExamples: Staff register with leaving dates and reasons | Exit conversation notes

text: How often does the owner meet staff or the management team to review sales, costs, cash and actions?
anchor0: Never
anchor1: Rarely, only when there is a problem
anchor2: Quarterly
anchor3: Monthly
anchor4: Monthly with written minutes and actions followed up
evidenceRequirement: Ask for minutes or an action list from the last three meetings.
evidenceExamples: Meeting minutes book | WhatsApp group summary of monthly review

text: Someone outside the business and the owner's family (adviser, mentor, board member) regularly challenges major decisions.
anchor0: No outside person is consulted
anchor1: Occasional chats with a friend
anchor2: An adviser is consulted occasionally on major decisions
anchor3: An advisory group or board meets at least twice a year
anchor4: Meets quarterly with minutes, tracked actions and at least one independent member
evidenceRequirement: Ask for minutes or advice notes and interview the adviser.
evidenceExamples: Advisory group minutes | Mentor session notes

text: Staff know in writing which decisions they can make without asking the owner (spending, pricing, hiring, discounts).
anchor0: The owner decides everything and nothing is stated
anchor1: Staff guess what they may decide
anchor2: Verbal limits are given for some decisions
anchor3: Written limits exist for spending, pricing and hiring
anchor4: Written limits signed by staff and reviewed within the last 12 months
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the written limits and ask two staff what they can decide alone.
evidenceExamples: Delegation of authority sheet | Manager appointment letter listing limits

text: Employees have a written statement of their job, pay, hours and leave.
anchor0: No written terms for anyone
anchor1: Terms are verbal only
anchor2: Written for some staff, for example only senior staff
anchor3: Written for all permanent staff
anchor4: Written for all staff, signed by both sides, copy held by the worker, and pay and leave records match
evidenceRequirement: Sample three employee contracts or statements and check pay and leave records.
evidenceExamples: Signed employment contract | Appointment letter with pay and leave terms

text: Basic safety measures are in place for the main hazards of the work.
anchor0: Obvious hazards are uncontrolled
anchor1: Hazards are known but nothing is done
anchor2: Some measures exist, such as a first aid box, without a routine
anchor3: Measures are in place for each main hazard, for example first aid, fire safety and protective gear
anchor4: As before, with incidents recorded and safety checks done at least quarterly
evidenceRequirement: Walk the premises and check safety items, and ask for any incident record.
evidenceExamples: First aid box and fire extinguisher with service date | Protective gear in use | Incident book

text: Registration certificates, licences, permits, leases, contracts and insurance papers are kept together in one safe place.
anchor0: Papers are scattered or lost
anchor1: Some are held but the owner does not know where all are
anchor2: Most are at the owner's home or shop with no copies
anchor3: All are in one place with a list of what is held
anchor4: In one place with scanned copies kept elsewhere, and the list is updated yearly
evidenceRequirement: Ask the owner to produce three named documents and the list.
evidenceExamples: Lever arch file of legal documents | Cloud folder of scanned certificates

text: Every sale of value is supported by an invoice, receipt or order note that the business keeps a copy of.
anchor0: No sales documents are issued
anchor1: Issued only when the customer asks
anchor2: Issued for some sales
anchor3: All credit sales and sales above a set amount have numbered documents
anchor4: All sales are documented in number order and checked against the ledger
evidenceRequirement: Inspect the invoice or receipt books for sequence and compare with the ledger.
evidenceExamples: Numbered receipt book | POS receipts or e-invoice records

text: The three most important routine tasks (for example cash handling, receiving goods, processing orders) each have written steps.
anchor0: None are written or explained
anchor1: Steps are known verbally only
anchor2: One task has written steps
anchor3: All three tasks have written steps
anchor4: All three are written, staff are trained on them and they were updated in the last 12 months
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the three step lists and ask a staff member to describe one.
evidenceExamples: Cash handling checklist | Goods received procedure sheet

text: Someone other than the owner can find and read the main business records.
anchor0: Only the owner knows where records are and how they work
anchor1: Only the owner can use the records
anchor2: One trusted person knows where they are
anchor3: A named records person has access and can use them
anchor4: A written index exists and two people have been trained to use the records
evidenceRequirement: Ask a second person to find a stated record while the owner is not helping.
evidenceExamples: Bookkeeper retrieves last month's ledger unaided | Index sheet to the filing system
riskTag: Records known only to the owner

text: Share of sales receipts that go through mobile money or a bank account.
anchor0: Under 10 percent
anchor1: 10 to 29 percent
anchor2: 30 to 49 percent
anchor3: 50 to 79 percent
anchor4: 80 percent or more
evidenceRequirement: Compare digital receipts on statements with total sales in the same month.
evidenceExamples: Mobile money merchant statement | Bank statement against sales ledger
riskTag: Most sales are in untraceable cash

text: The business has a bank account or mobile money business wallet in the business's name that is in regular use.
anchor0: No account or wallet in the business's name
anchor2: Account or wallet exists but has no transactions in the last three months
anchor4: Account or wallet in the business's name shows transactions in each of the last three months
evidenceRequirement: Review statements from the last three months in the business's name.
evidenceExamples: Bank statement in business name | MoMo merchant account statement

text: Sales and accounts are kept in a spreadsheet or software, not only on paper or in the owner's head.
anchor0: Nothing is kept in any digital form
anchor1: Notes on a phone only
anchor2: Spreadsheet used occasionally
anchor3: Spreadsheet or software used for the ledger every month
anchor4: Accounting or point of sale software with backups, and reports used every month
evidenceRequirement: Open the file or software and check entries and dates.
evidenceExamples: Excel ledger | Accounting software or POS reports

text: Customers can reach the business through a dedicated business phone number, WhatsApp Business or email address.
anchor0: No way for customers to reach the business except by visiting
anchor1: Only the owner's personal number is available
anchor2: A business number exists but is not displayed
anchor3: A dedicated number or email is displayed on signage, cards or social media
anchor4: Dedicated contact is displayed and enquiries are answered within a set time and logged
evidenceRequirement: Check signage, social media page and send a test enquiry.
evidenceExamples: WhatsApp Business profile | Banner showing the business phone number

text: The business tracks a small set of numbers every month (sales, gross margin, cash balance, money owed by customers, stock).
anchor0: No numbers are tracked
anchor1: Sales only
anchor2: Sales and cash
anchor3: Four or more measures in writing every month
anchor4: Monthly dashboard with targets and a trend over six months
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the last three months' figures.
evidenceExamples: Monthly scorecard | Notebook of monthly key numbers

text: In the last six months the owner has made a decision that was clearly based on the recorded figures.
anchor0: Decisions are made by gut feeling alone
anchor1: Records exist but are not consulted
anchor2: The owner occasionally looks at figures
anchor3: Two decisions in the last six months can be traced to the figures
anchor4: Figures are used routinely and decisions are written with the numbers behind them
evidenceRequirement: Ask for two decisions and the figures used, and check dates.
evidenceExamples: Dropped a slow product after stock figures | Raised a price after margin calculation

text: The owner compares this year's results with last year's at least once a year.
anchor0: No records to compare
anchor1: Compares from memory only
anchor2: Compares sales only
anchor3: Compares sales, costs and profit once a year
anchor4: Compares every quarter and writes down the reasons for changes
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the comparison and the reasons noted.
evidenceExamples: Year on year sales and costs table | Annual review notes

text: At least each quarter, actual results are compared with the plan or budget and the differences are explained in writing.
anchor0: Never compared
anchor1: Compared informally once a year
anchor2: Compared informally each quarter
anchor3: Written comparison each quarter
anchor4: Written comparison each month with corrective actions closed
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the last two comparisons and the actions that followed.
evidenceExamples: Budget versus actual sheet | Quarterly review note

text: The business is legally registered and its registration is current (certificate valid, annual renewal or annual return up to date).
anchor0: Not registered with the Registrar General's Department
anchor2: Registered, but the annual renewal or annual return is overdue or the details are out of date
anchor4: Valid certificate in the business's name, with annual renewal or annual return up to date
evidenceRequirement: Inspect the certificate and the latest renewal or annual return acknowledgement.
evidenceExamples: Business name or company registration certificate | Registrar General annual return or renewal receipt

text: All tax returns that fell due in the last 12 months have been filed on time with the Ghana Revenue Authority.
anchor0: No TIN, or no returns have been filed
anchor1: Has a TIN but has filed no returns
anchor2: Some returns have been filed
anchor3: All returns have been filed but some were late
anchor4: All returns filed on time, with GRA acknowledgements kept
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the TIN and filing acknowledgements, and check dates against due dates.
evidenceExamples: GRA portal filing acknowledgement | Tax clearance certificate
riskTag: Tax returns not filed on time

text: The owner can say which GRA taxes apply to the business (income tax, VAT, PAYE, withholding) and keeps a calendar of due dates.
anchor0: Unaware which taxes apply
anchor1: Knows only about income tax
anchor2: Knows the main taxes but has no calendar
anchor3: Has a calendar of the taxes that apply, with due dates
anchor4: Calendar kept, payments tracked with receipts, and advice taken from a tax practitioner or GRA
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the calendar and the payment receipts for the last quarter.
evidenceExamples: Tax calendar on the office wall | Spreadsheet of tax due dates and payment dates

text: Employee SSNIT contributions and PAYE are paid by the due date every month.
anchor0: Employees are not registered with SSNIT and PAYE is not deducted
anchor1: Registered but contributions are in arrears
anchor2: Paid, but often late
anchor3: Paid on time in most months, with proof
anchor4: Paid on time every month for 12 months, with SSNIT and GRA proof
evidenceRequirement: Ask for SSNIT contribution schedules, payment proof and PAYE payment evidence for the last six months.
evidenceExamples: SSNIT employer contribution report | GRA PAYE payment acknowledgement

text: Important sales and supply arrangements (large customers, key suppliers, premises) are in written agreements.
anchor0: No written agreements
anchor1: Everything is verbal
anchor2: Some arrangements are in messages or notes only
anchor3: Written, signed agreements exist for large buyers and key suppliers
anchor4: Signed agreements cover price, payment, delivery and ending the contract, and are filed and reviewed
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the agreements with the three largest customers or suppliers.
evidenceExamples: Supply agreement | Signed local purchase order terms

text: The business has a right to use its premises for at least the next 12 months, shown in a lease, tenancy agreement or title.
anchor0: No right to the premises and a risk of being moved
anchor1: A verbal arrangement only
anchor2: A written agreement exists but expires within six months
anchor3: A written lease or tenancy valid for at least 12 months
anchor4: Title, or a lease of three years or more
evidenceRequirement: Inspect the lease, tenancy agreement or title document and check dates.
evidenceExamples: Tenancy agreement | Land title or allocation letter

text: The business has taken a step to stop its brand name, logo or product design being copied.
anchor0: Unaware this is possible and copying has occurred
anchor1: Aware but has done nothing
anchor2: Business name registered only
anchor3: Trademark or design application filed, or staff have signed confidentiality terms
anchor4: Trademark or design granted, or confidentiality is in force and breaches are handled
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the registration, application or signed confidentiality terms.
evidenceExamples: Trademark filing receipt | Staff confidentiality clause in contract

text: The owner has written a list of the main risks to the business (fire, theft, price changes, loss of a key customer, illness) and what will be done about each.
anchor0: Has not thought about risks
anchor1: Aware of risks but nothing is discussed or written
anchor2: An informal list exists
anchor3: A written list names the main risks, an owner and an action for each
anchor4: Written list reviewed at least yearly and after any incident, with actions checked
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the risk list and the last review date.
evidenceExamples: Risk register | Notebook page of risks and responses

text: The business holds valid insurance for its biggest insurable risks (stock, premises, vehicles, workers).
anchor0: No insurance of any kind
anchor1: Knows the options but holds none
anchor2: Holds only compulsory cover such as vehicle third party
anchor3: Main assets and stock are insured with valid policies
anchor4: Valid policies with values checked at least yearly
evidenceRequirement: Inspect the policy documents, the cover amounts and the expiry dates.
evidenceExamples: Fire and stock insurance policy | Motor insurance certificate

text: Valuable stock and cash are protected by physical controls (locks, safe, limited keyholders, cash banked regularly).
anchor0: Stock and cash are left exposed
anchor1: Locked at night only
anchor2: Locked, with some limits on who has access
anchor3: Secured storage with a limited number of keyholders and cash banked at least weekly
anchor4: As before, plus daily banking and a record of access and incidents
evidenceRequirement: Inspect storage, ask who holds keys and check banking dates.
evidenceExamples: Locked store with keyholder list | Deposit slips showing regular banking
riskTag: Stock and cash exposed to theft

text: Written steps exist for keeping key activities running after a disruption (fire, power cut, illness of a key person, loss of premises).
anchor0: No plan of any kind
anchor1: Owner has a plan in mind only
anchor2: Informal notes for one scenario
anchor3: A written plan for the main disruptions with a contact list
anchor4: Written plan tested or practised within the last 12 months
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the plan and any record of a practice or real use.
evidenceExamples: Continuity checklist with contacts | Notes from a power cut drill

text: Business records and customer data are backed up so they could be recovered after loss of a phone, computer or the premises.
anchor0: No backup; one copy only
anchor1: A second copy is kept in the same place
anchor2: Occasional backups with no routine
anchor3: Monthly backup kept in a separate place (cloud, other premises) and recovery within a week is possible
anchor4: At least weekly off site backup and a recovery test done in the last 12 months, recovering within a day
evidenceRequirement: Ask to see the backup and the date of the last one, and ask for a test restore.
evidenceExamples: Cloud backup log | External drive with dated copies kept off site

text: The business handles personal data about customers and staff in line with the Data Protection Act, including registration with the Data Protection Commission.
anchor0: Unaware of the rules; personal data is on open or shared phones and papers
anchor1: Aware of the rules but has taken no steps
anchor2: Basic security (lock, passcodes) but not registered
anchor3: Registered with the Data Protection Commission and basic security in place
anchor4: Registration renewed, written data handling rules, staff briefed and a way to answer data requests
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the registration certificate and inspect how personal data is stored.
evidenceExamples: Data Protection Commission registration certificate | Locked cabinet for staff files and password protected customer list
riskTag: Personal data not protected or registered

text: Electricity, fuel and water use and cost are tracked every month.
anchor0: Not tracked
anchor1: Bills are paid but not compared
anchor2: Bills are kept and total cost is known
anchor3: Monthly cost is compared and the biggest users are identified
anchor4: Units used are tracked against output and a reduction target is set
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the last six months of utility bills and the comparison.
evidenceExamples: ECG electricity bills and prepaid meter records | Fuel purchase log
riskTag: Energy and water use not tracked

text: In the last 12 months the business has taken at least one action to cut energy or water use (LED lighting, solar, efficient equipment, repairing leaks).
anchor0: No action and none planned
anchor1: An action is being considered
anchor2: One low cost action has been taken
anchor3: Two or more actions taken and savings estimated
anchor4: Savings measured and further actions planned
evidenceRequirement: Inspect the measures and compare bills before and after.
evidenceExamples: Solar panel or LED bulbs installed | Leak repair receipts

text: Waste (packaging, scrap, used oil, chemicals, electronic waste, organic waste) is sorted, reused or disposed of safely.
anchor0: Waste is dumped or burnt in the open
anchor1: Left for general collection with no separation
anchor2: Some waste is reused or collected
anchor3: Waste is sorted, reused or sold, and hazardous items go to an approved collector
anchor4: As before, with waste measured and reduced
evidenceRequirement: Inspect waste handling and ask for collector or buyer receipts for hazardous or recyclable items.
evidenceExamples: Separate bins for scrap and plastics | Receipt from approved waste collector

text: The business has taken a practical step against a climate hazard that affects it (flood, heat, drought, storm, power outages).
anchor0: Has not considered climate hazards
anchor1: Has considered them but done nothing
anchor2: Has a plan but not yet acted
anchor3: One practical step is in place, such as drainage, shade, water storage or backup power
anchor4: Several steps in place and reviewed after each event
evidenceRequirement: Inspect the measure and ask what hazard it addresses and when it was done.
evidenceExamples: Raised storage racks against flooding | Backup power supply for a cold room

text: Women and men doing the same work in the business are paid equally and have the same chance of promotion.
anchor0: Clear pay gaps or exclusion from promotion
anchor1: Inequality is known and accepted
anchor2: No rule on equal pay, but no known gap
anchor3: Pay scales are the same for the same role and have been checked
anchor4: Pay and role data by gender are reviewed yearly and gaps acted on
evidenceRequirement: Compare pay for the same role across women and men and ask staff about promotion.
evidenceExamples: Payroll listing pay by role | Promotion decisions in the last two years

text: Both women and people under 35 hold jobs with real responsibility (supervisor, technician, manager), not only casual or lowest paid roles.
anchor0: Neither group holds any role of responsibility, or any role at all
anchor1: Both groups work only in casual or lowest paid roles
anchor2: One of the two groups holds a role of responsibility
anchor3: Both groups hold at least one role of responsibility
anchor4: Both groups hold several such roles and a training or apprenticeship route is recorded
evidenceRequirement: Review the staff list by role, sex and age band and ask about training routes.
evidenceExamples: Staff list showing supervisors by sex and age | Apprenticeship records
riskTag: Women and youth excluded from responsibility

text: Women who own, work in or help run the business take part in decisions about how its income is spent.
anchor0: Women have no say in decisions
anchor1: Women are consulted rarely
anchor2: Women are consulted but the owner decides alone
anchor3: Women take part in business decisions that affect them
anchor4: Women confirm, when asked separately, that they take part in decisions and control the income they earn
evidenceRequirement: Speak separately to the women connected to the business about their role in decisions and income.
evidenceExamples: Wife or female partner confirms joint decisions on spending | Female staff describe how bonuses and tasks are decided

text: The workplace has a rule against harassment and a safe way for staff to report it.
anchor0: No rule and harassment is tolerated
anchor1: A verbal rule only
anchor2: An informal open door with the owner
anchor3: A written rule known to staff, with a named person to report to
anchor4: Written rule, staff briefed, and a reporting process that is used and logged
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the written rule and ask two staff how they would report a concern.
evidenceExamples: Staff handbook clause on harassment | Notice naming the person to report to
riskTag: No harassment rule or reporting route

text: The owner has written down what the business would do if monthly sales fell by a quarter for three months.
anchor0: Has no idea what would be done
anchor1: Would cut staff or borrow personally, with no plan
anchor2: Actions are described verbally
anchor3: A written response with triggers and cost cuts
anchor4: Written response that has been rehearsed or used before
evidenceRequirement: Ask for the written response and when it was last reviewed.
evidenceExamples: Page of cost cuts and triggers | Plan used during a previous sales drop
riskTag: No plan for a sales drop

text: Share of sales in the last 12 months that came from the largest single product or service line.
anchor0: Above 90 percent
anchor1: 76 to 90 percent
anchor2: 61 to 75 percent
anchor3: 41 to 60 percent
anchor4: 40 percent or less
evidenceRequirement: Calculate from sales records by product or service line.
evidenceExamples: Sales by product report | Ledger totals by product line

text: The owner belongs to a business association, cooperative, trade group or peer network and has attended its meetings.
anchor0: Not a member of any network and works alone
anchor1: Member but not active
anchor2: Attended one meeting in the last six months
anchor3: Attended two or more meetings in the last six months
anchor4: Active, and has used the network for a concrete benefit in the last 12 months (referral, shared purchase, guarantee)
evidenceRequirement: Ask for membership proof and a recent benefit received.
evidenceExamples: Association membership card | Group purchasing receipt

text: At least two people can perform each critical task (taking orders, bookkeeping, production, delivery).
anchor0: Each task depends on one person and nobody can cover
anchor1: Informal cover for some tasks only
anchor2: Backup named for one critical task
anchor3: Backups named for all critical tasks
anchor4: Backups named and tested through cross training in the last 12 months
evidenceRequirement: Ask who covers each critical task and when cover was last used.
evidenceExamples: Cover roster | Second person trained to do invoicing
riskTag: Critical tasks depend on one person
